think:
1. Core Clinical Tension: A 45-year-old male renal transplant recipient maintained on prednisolone and cyclosporine presents with two massive, rapidly growing cauliflower-like tumoral lesions on his wrist and lower leg. In an immunocompromised transplant patient, such exuberant exophytic masses mimic post-transplant lymphoproliferative disorders, aggressive cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma, or opportunistic deep fungal infections, concealing dramatic reactivation of previously indolent cutaneous leishmaniasis acquired two years earlier in endemic Iran.
2. Admission Breakpoint: The admission breakpoint falls immediately upon dermatologic triage and physical examination describing the large cauliflower-like cutaneous tumors in the setting of post-transplant immunosuppression, prior to slit-skin smear cytology, leishmanin skin testing, and incisional punch biopsy.
3. Differential Distinctions: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma and other post-transplant neoplasms show marked nuclear atypia, pleomorphism, and invasive malignant nests rather than reactive pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia; deep fungal infections (e.g., chromoblastomycosis) demonstrate fungal elements on periodic acid-Schiff/Gomori methenamine silver stains. Reactivation of cutaneous leishmaniasis is established by identification of characteristic Leishman-Donovan bodies within dermal histiocytes on Giemsa-stained slit smear and skin biopsy.
case_prompt:
A 45-year-old Iranian man with a history of end-stage diabetic nephropathy who underwent renal transplantation seven months prior presents to the dermatology clinic for evaluation of two rapidly growing, tumoral cutaneous lesions. Following transplantation, he was maintained on immunosuppressive therapy consisting of oral prednisolone (50 mg daily) and cyclosporine (7.5 mg/kg daily). Approximately two years prior to admission, following travel to Natanz in Isfahan province, Iran, he had noted two small papular skin lesions measuring 2 mm by 5 mm on his left wrist and right anterior lower leg (shin), which had remained stable, indolent, and untreated. However, several weeks after the initiation of calcineurin inhibitor and corticosteroid immunosuppressive therapy following transplantation, these quiescent papules underwent dramatic, rapid expansion.

On physical examination, the patient is afebrile with normal vital signs. Dermatologic examination reveals two massive, cauliflower-like, exophytic tumoral masses: one measuring 3 cm by 4 cm by 5 cm on the left wrist, and a second measuring 4 cm by 5 cm by 6 cm on the right anterior shin. The lesions are vegetating with surface ulceration and crusting. Systemic physical examination is otherwise unremarkable with no palpable regional lymphadenopathy or peripheral stigmata of systemic infection.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Cutaneous Squamous Cell Carcinoma / Post-Transplant Malignancy
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Organ transplant recipients on prolonged calcineurin inhibitor and corticosteroid therapy have a massively elevated risk of aggressive cutaneous malignancies; the rapidly enlarging, cauliflower-like exophytic tumoral masses with epidermal pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia strongly suggested squamous cell carcinoma or Kaposi sarcoma. However, histopathology demonstrated reactive hyperplastic changes without malignant cytological atypia or invasive neoplastic cells.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Histopathological examination of the biopsy obtained specimens demonstrated ulcerative changes and irregular acanthosis in the epidermis, namely, pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia. In dermis infiltration of lymphocyte, plasma cell and histiocyte with multinucleated Giant cell were shown. Leishman bodies were seen in histiocytes

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Vegetating, chronic verrucous cutaneous tumors in an immunosuppressed renal allograft recipient raised high suspicion for opportunistic dimorphic or dematiaceous fungal infection (such as chromoblastomycosis, sporotrichosis) or atypical mycobacteriosis; ruled out by absence of fungal structures and specific detection of intracellular protozoan amastigotes.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A slit-skin smear showed leishman bodies in Giemsa preparations... Leishman bodies were seen in histiocytes, especially in the specimen obtained from the lower leg lesion (Figure 3).

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Diagnostic Pivot: Reactivation of Cutaneous Leishmaniasis Post-Transplantation
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The diagnostic breakthrough was achieved when Giemsa-stained slit-skin smear and skin biopsy demonstrated dense dermal histiocytic infiltration containing numerous intracellular Leishman bodies (amastigotes), corroborated by a positive Montenegro skin test (5 mm induration), proving post-transplant reactivation of dormant leishmanial infection. The patient achieved complete lesion cure following parenteral sodium stibogluconate and local cryotherapy.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: A slit-skin smear showed leishman bodies in Giemsa preparations. The leishmanin skin test (Montenegro) was positive with 5 mm induration... With regard to the clinical and histopathological findings, the diagnosis of reactivation of CL was made. After admission to our dermatology department, he was treated with 800 mg/day IV sodium stibogluconate (Pentostam, pentavalent antimonials) for 3 weeks.

editor_comments: Breakpoint established before slit-skin smear, skin testing, and biopsy. Prompt excludes all mentions of leishmaniasis, CL, or parasite bodies from the presentation.
